title: Soufflé orbits benchmark: naive versus semi-naive evaluation
explanation: Soufflé's orbits.dl benchmark computes the transitive closure of a seed relation, orbits (the orbits of the seed relation under composition), together with intermediate (a two-step composition of orbits with itself) and satellite (orbit pairs not reachable by such an intermediate two-step path) built on top of it — a graph-composition closure computation. The triple compares naive versus semi-naive evaluation of the whole program, claiming all three output relations agree between the two strategies.
preInWords: True; no precondition constrains the inputs.
postInWords: The naively computed intermediate, orbits, and satellite relations each equal their semi-naive counterparts.
sides: naive translation of orbits.dl (Soufflé benchmark suite)
semi-naive translation of orbits.dl (Soufflé benchmark suite)
sourceProgram: orbits.dl of the Soufflé benchmark suite (naive translation)
encoding: canonical five-declaration form; programs run in sequence and merged by Hoare.preprocess; compiled sides are naive-compiler output pinned by Fidelity/ (decide +kernel); hand-written sides are the retired corpus commands verbatim under a bijective rename of relation names

datalog.label: normalized Soufflé source (orbits.dl of the Soufflé benchmark suite (naive translation))
datalog.text:
.decl orbits_seed(v0:symbol, v1:symbol) input
.decl orbits(v0:symbol, v1:symbol) output
.decl intermediate(v0:symbol, v1:symbol) output
.decl satellite(v0:symbol, v1:symbol) output

orbits(V0, V1) :- orbits_seed(V0, V1).
orbits(X, Y) :- orbits(X, Z), orbits(Z, Y).
satellite(X, Y) :- orbits(X, Y), !intermediate(X, Y).
intermediate(X, Y) :- orbits(X, Z), orbits(Z, Y).
